name: Volatility-Targeted Time-Series Momentum
note: The sign of the trailing lb-bar return is the entire entry condition, re-evaluated only every hold bars and held untouched in between - the monthly rebalance of the published rule, in bars. Everything else is risk: ex-ante annualised volatility from an EWMA of squared returns with a centre of mass of com_frac*lb bars (0.25*252 = 63, the paper's 60), annualised by the bar rate inferred from the timestamps, gives the target leverage vol_target/sigma capped at lev_cap. LIMITATION, stated plainly: the shared harness sizes every family identically, so the continuously varying vol-inverse NOTIONAL - which is the idea's real content - cannot be expressed. What survives is the part of it that changes the trade decision rather than its size: the book goes FLAT whenever the vol-scaled target leverage falls below min_lev, so exposure is cut by a volatility spike before any price signal moves, plus the paper's optional intramonth overlay that flattens on a drawdown from the position's high-water mark beyond dd_mult*sigma/sqrt(12).
source: Moskowitz, T.J., Ooi, Y.H., and Pedersen, L.H., 'Time Series Momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 104(2), 2012, pp. 228-250 - sign of the past 12-month excess return, one-month holding period, position scaled to a 40% annualised volatility target using an exponentially weighted ex-ante volatility estimate with a 60-day centre of mass.
